WEDE5020 Debugging Lab

Fix seven problems from the repair café website. Work in a scratch folder in VS Code. Copy each starter into its own test page, reproduce the problem, change one thing and retest before revealing the worked fix.

Keep a short test log with the symptom, cause, change and retest result. Use Elements for HTML and CSS, Console for JavaScript, and Network for failed file requests.

HTML . Fix a broken navigation link HTML . Connect a label to its field CSS . Stop a card from overflowing on mobile CSS . Fix a selector that targets the wrong element JavaScript . Make the hours button work JavaScript . Show feedback when a filter finds nothing GitHub Pages . Restore a stylesheet on the published site

1. Fix a broken navigation link

Open index.html in the browser and follow the Visit link. The real file is pages/visit.html beside the homepage’s pages folder.

Broken starter

<a href="page/visit.html">Visit</a>

Expected result Clicking Visit opens pages/visit.html.

Show hint

Compare each directory segment in href with the project tree.

Show worked fix 
<a href="pages/visit.html">Visit</a>

The link is relative to index.html. From the nested Visit page, a link back home would use ../index.html.

2. Connect a label to its field

Paste the fragment into a practice page. Click the label and observe whether focus moves to the field.

Broken starter

<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input id="contact" name="email" type="email">

Expected result Clicking the label focuses the email input, which has the accessible name Email address.

Show hint

Compare the label’s for value with the input’s id.

Show worked fix 
<label for="contact">Email address</label>
<input id="contact" name="email" type="email">

The attribute for references id. The name attribute identifies the field in submitted data.

3. Stop a card from overflowing on mobile

Paste this into an HTML file and set the viewport to 320px in DevTools. Look for sideways scrolling.

Broken starter

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<style>
  .card { width: 420px; padding: 24px; border: 1px solid; }
</style>
<article class="card">Saturday repair session</article>

Expected result The card fits its container at phone width and has a maximum width of 420px.

Show hint

A fixed width can exceed the viewport. The default box model also adds padding and borders to the stated width.

Show worked fix 
.card {
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 420px;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: 24px;
  border: 1px solid;
}

Replace only the rule inside style. Check the Computed box model, then confirm the page fits at 320px and 768px.

4. Fix a selector that targets the wrong element

Open the fragment in the browser. In Elements, select the paragraph and see which CSS rules matched it.

Broken starter

<style>
  #notice { font-weight: 700; }
</style>
<p class="notice">Bring your charger.</p>

Expected result The notice appears bold through the CSS rule.

Show hint

Does # select an ID or a class?

Show worked fix 
.notice { font-weight: 700; }

The dot matches class="notice". Keep the class so more than one notice can reuse the rule.

5. Make the hours button work

Run this fragment, open DevTools Console and click the button. Read the first error and the line it points to.

Broken starter

<button id="show-hours" type="button">Show hours</button>
<p id="hours" role="status"></p>
<script>
  const button = document.querySelector('#showHours');
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    document.querySelector('#hours').textContent = 'Saturday, 10:00-13:00';
  });
</script>

Expected result Clicking or pressing Enter on the button displays the Saturday hours.

Show hint

Check what querySelector returns when no element matches.

Show worked fix 
const button = document.querySelector('#show-hours');
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#hours').textContent = 'Saturday, 10:00-13:00';
});

The ID and selector must match. Replace the JavaScript inside script and retest with mouse and keyboard.

6. Show feedback when a filter finds nothing

Paste the fragment into a page. Search for fan, then radio, and note what appears below the buttons.

Broken starter

<button type="button" data-query="fan">Find fan</button>
<button type="button" data-query="radio">Find radio</button>
<p id="results" role="status"></p>
<script>
  const items = ['fan', 'lamp'];
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-query]').forEach(button => {
    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
      const matches = items.filter(item => item === button.dataset.query);
      document.querySelector('#results').textContent = matches.join(', ');
    });
  });
</script>

Expected result Find fan shows fan. Find radio shows No matching repair items.

Show hint

What does join return for an empty array?

Show worked fix 
const results = document.querySelector('#results');
results.textContent = matches.length
  ? matches.join(', ')
  : 'No matching repair items.';

Replace the results assignment inside the click handler with this block. Try fan, radio, then fan again to verify the message updates each time.

7. Restore a stylesheet on the published site

Assume the site lives at https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/repair-cafe/ and the stylesheet is committed at css/Site.css. Inspect the CSS request in Network and compare its URL with that path.

Broken starter

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/site.css">

Expected result The published homepage loads its stylesheet from /repair-cafe/css/Site.css.

Show hint

A leading slash starts at the domain root. The filename also has a capital S.

Show worked fix 
<link rel="stylesheet" href="./css/Site.css">

Use this from the homepage. From pages/visit.html use ../css/Site.css. After pushing and deploying, reload and confirm Network shows a successful stylesheet response.
